pr_title: sensor: fix: decouple Sensor Async API request from its execution
pr_body:
### Description
This PR introduces a shim layer to decouple the Sensor Read Async API from its execution. It achieves this by introducing the RTIO Workqueues service, relying on P4WQ's, and a pool of pre-allocated work items to process the requests.

Fixes #73676

### Changes
- Add RTIO Workqueues service.
- Add testsuite to validate RTIO Workqueues service.
- Incorporate RTIO Work requests to all sensor drivers implementing the submit API (this is the bug-fix).

### Testing
- Sensors Generic Testsuite
``` console
twister -p native_sim --inline-logs -vvv -s tests/drivers/build_all/sensor/sensors.generic_test
```
- RTIO Workq testsuite
``` console
twister -p native_sim --inline-logs -vvv -s tests/subsys/rtio/workq/rtio.workq
```
- Shell sample
``` console
west build -b croxel_cx1825/nrf52840 samples/shell/shell_module -- -DCONFIG_SENSOR -- -DCONFIG_SENSOR_SHELL=y
```
- DHT Polling sample
``` console
west build -b <target> samples/sensor/dht_polling
```

EDIT 240621: This is no longer an issue with the latest approach.

@teburd Thanks for your feedback!

Overall, I don't have a strong opinion: I think both are valid and have their pros/cons. 

Some thoughts:

Since this is a temporary solution, my preference would be to:
- Avoid duplication as much as practical, and
- Make it easy to remove after it's no longer needed.

>  I do wonder though if we're going to be working around functional sensor drivers with this.
 
 That's true. With this existing approach we're applying the workaround for all implementations: _good and bad_. However, this may not be significant for the upcoming release as I don't think any of the existing in-tree implementations meet the criteria of "good example" (maybe I'm wrong and I'm missing out :') ).

> How do we help guide sensor developers with this change to do the right thing?

This one is a tough question, as hiding it from the common sensor path may also mean it's "more" exposed to the sensor drivers - e.g: developers may think that since existing in-tree `.submit` are implemented using the P4WQ + blocking-handler this is expected way to work and we start seeing more instances following that pattern.

Ideally, these would be some suggestions on how we could make this better:
- **Improve documentation**: of `sensor_submit_t` to indicate driver implementors these shall follow asynchronous/non-blocking pattern (and RTIO-based). P.S: I know you're probably working on this one!
-  **Consolidate Reference Implementation**: we basically "fix" one instance to be completely non-blocking and utilize RTIO API calls (counting on #73869 coming up soon).

However, this doesn't seem like a feasible approach considering the stage of the upcoming release.

Having said all of that - let's go with whichever one we feel most comfortable with and let's focus on the path moving forward. I'm happy to take this PR either way: LMK if, after reading through these comments, you still lean towards your proposition and I'll spend some time thinking how to restructure it to avoid duplication and meet this goal at the same time.

There's 4 drivers in the tree (5 if you include the fallback) that effectively block on submit. I don't think it'd be too much work to reuse p4wq with a helper to convert the async task.

Exposing the p4wq shim here as it is, only to delete it right after seems wrong. I'd rather us provide it as a proper tool, noting that it is a workaround/shim for drivers to use. I get the idea of reducing code duplication, I'm believe its still going to be pretty minimal patch even moving some of this to the 4-5 drivers in the tree today.

I think we need some others to chime in here though to perhaps break the tie @MaureenHelm @yperess
Sounds reasonable - I'll work on refactoring it, thanks!

This is looking super nice, I'd actually go ahead and simply call it rtio_p4wq rather than rtio_async_shim as its more widely useable than simply as a shim. There will likely always be blocking actions that may wish to be done asynchronously. I know that's going back on what I said earlier about it being a shim, but seeing it here I think it is a proper tool now to solve a problem and should be named as such.

Basically, from how I've read io_uring this is more or less how io_uring works internally (thread pool).

Great job! +1 from me with/without rename, up to you on that one.

issue_context.title: Sensor Async Read API implementation is synchronous/blocking
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
As discussed on 240603 Sensors WG meeting, the Sensor Async Read API `sensor_read_async_mempool` execution path is synchronous for most if not all drivers instances in-tree.
Even though the performance-optimized version of this API is conditioned on RTIO availability for Bus drivers (see #67328 and #67327), we should still comply with the API description and make this API invocation Asynchrnous and Non-blocking. That way, users can start leveraging the new Sensor API in their applications, and take advantage of the optimizations once introduced.

**Examples of the synchronous/blocking pattern in-tree:**
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/127cb9edb6c6594e2f09dea7efb335db3cb1f43a/drivers/sensor/tdk/icm42688/icm42688_rtio.c#L17
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/127cb9edb6c6594e2f09dea7efb335db3cb1f43a/drivers/sensor/asahi_kasei/akm09918c/akm09918c_async.c#L31
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/127cb9edb6c6594e2f09dea7efb335db3cb1f43a/drivers/sensor/bosch/bma4xx/bma4xx.c#L341 

**Impact**
Users can't rely on the asynchronous nature of `sensor_read_async_mempool` API. For instance, invoking this API inside a time-sensitive context would not work (e.g: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/127cb9edb6c6594e2f09dea7efb335db3cb1f43a/subsys/sensing/sensor_mgmt.c#L288).

**Proposed Solution**
Decouple the sensor read submission from its execution. From many approaches that could work, I'm thinking of:
- Have a separate workqueue for the sensor drivers, which all sensors share with each other.
- Each sensor instance has an associated work-item that executes the read procedure.
- The asynchronous execution path ends up by submitting this item in the workqueue, which after completed, signals the RTIO item completion.
- This implies that even the fallback implementation for drivers using fetch/get API (`sensor_submit_fallback`) will comply with being non-blocking/asynchronous.
- Once the sensor drivers are implemented in a non-blocking fashion, this decoupling can be removed gracefully.

Hi @ubieda. Adding some of my thoughts here, as there is discussion  IMO RTIO should handle the interrupt request in it's own context (i.e, Threads, work queue for RTIO operation)as existing RTIO does not have any. This potentially avoid thread/work handler usage in every sensor driver implementation. Is there any way to handle the time series data from the sensor using the RTIO, don't how it is feasible.

Hi @karthi012, thanks for your feedback!

> IMO RTIO should handle the interrupt request in it's own context (i.e, Threads, work queue for RTIO operation)as existing RTIO does not have any.

As I understand it, the ideal scenario is that all sensor drivers implementing the `sensor_read_async_mempool` API  rely on the RTIO bus drivers, without the need of additional contexts (workqueue, thread, etc). These RTIO bus driver implementations would handle the transactions in a non-blocking/asynchronous manner.

To do that, however, there are multiple pieces that need to be in place and that takes time. This bug only attempts to address the immediate need for this API to be compliant with its description (being async, non-blocking) so the expectation can be met for the next release.

Introducing the shim at the RTIO bus drivers layer (which is what is suggested here: #73869) is planned after this release. 

> Is there any way to handle the time series data from the sensor using the RTIO, don't how it is feasible.

I'm not sure I understand what you mean by "handling time-series data". Could you expand on this?
@ubieda Thanks for your clarification. Please ignore time series data handling.
